Subject: URGENT: Launch weekend rate smoothing request

Hi Hannah,

Quick note — we’ve just completed a load preview for our production rollout (internal) and the traffic shape for the weekend spike is much spikier than we estimated: multiple concurrent workflows will hit the /generate endpoint for short bursts (2–5s) every few minutes. The net effect is a lot of short-lived bursts rather than a smooth steady rate.

Our platform depends on low tail-latency; the current fairshare throttles and burst ceilings in our contract appear likely to cause request failures and degraded UX during the first 24–72 hours of launch.

Can Redwood temporarily relax the burst ceiling and reduce the fairness penalty for Ventana for the initial launch window? Specifically we’re asking for: 
- a temporary smoothing window that treats short bursts as a single higher-capacity request for 48 hours
- a 2.5x burst allowance vs. baseline committed throughput for that period
- an explicit fallback plan if resource pressure rises (we can route some non-critical background jobs to off-peak times)

I attached a short traffic plan with expected QPS, percentiles and example payloads.

We appreciate this is an exception request; happy to jump on a call with your ops/infra team to walk through the traffic. Please advise next steps and any info you need from our side.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao

Short update from infra side after a quick triage of the traffic sheet: the pattern is exactly the sort that triggers fairness smoothing today (high short-lived concurrency). We have two pragmatic options: 

1) Policy-level smoothing (preferred): create a temporary per-customer policy that aggregates short bursts into a sliding window token bucket ("burst_smoothing_ventana_Xh"). That lets us avoid increasing reserved capacity but reduces fairness penalties for Ventana for a fixed window. Implementation time: ~3–6 hours to create, test in staging, and roll. Downside: while active, Ventana will effectively consume a larger share of free pool capacity which could affect other customers during coincident peaks.

2) Reserved-capacity uplift: spin up a short-lived dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs) for the 48–72 hour window. This is more predictable but costs more and requires procurement signoff if we charge it back.

Technical caveats:
- We can tie smoothing to payload signatures (model variant + request path) to limit scope.
- We should put an automated backstop: if cluster pressure exceeds X% for Y minutes, the policy auto-reverts and routes Ventana to the next-compatible model variant with higher quantization.

I’ve sketched a policy draft and test checklist (policy-draft.json). My recommendation: go with option 1 + automated backstop, and include option 2 as fallback if we detect sustained pressure.

— Markus
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime

Hi Sanjay — following our internal review, Redwood will provision a temporary per-customer rate-smoothing policy for Ventana with the following terms: 

- Window: 2026-09-02 00:00 UTC -> 2026-09-05 00:00 UTC (72 hours)
- Effective burst allowance: up to 2.0x baseline committed throughput aggregated via sliding-window smoothing
- Auto-backstop: if cluster memory/GPUs under sustained pressure (> 80% for 10m), the smoothing policy auto-reverts and Ventana’s traffic will be routed to a compatible, lower-cost model variant; we’ll notify your on-call and provide a minute-by-minute trace.
- Fallback coordination: Ventana agreed to route non-critical batch jobs to off-peak; we will throttle background paths first.

Attached is a short SLA addendum draft (ventana-sla-addendum-draft.pdf) that documents the carveout, audit logs we’ll provide, and the exact metrics we’ll monitor. Note the final addendum requires sign-off from legal/finance; Ben will follow up with the contract bits and a DocuSign link.

3) Sanjay: confirm acceptance of the 2.0x level and the start window.
